candidates.text: To uphold the Government's contentions here, we would have to pile inference upon inference
candidates.speaker: Rehnquist

candidates.text: Section 922(q) is a criminal statute that by its terms has nothing to do with `commerce' or any sort of economic enterprise
candidates.speaker: Rehnquist
phrases: essential part of a larger regulation of economic activity

candidates.text: Were the Federal Government to take over the regulation of entire areas of traditional state concern
candidates.speaker: Kennedy, concurring
phrases: boundaries between the spheres of federal and state authority would blur

candidates.text: Upholding this legislation would do no more than simply recognize that Congress had a `rational basis'
candidates.speaker: Breyer, dissenting
phrases: significant connection between guns in or near schools

candidates.text: Put simply, much if not all of Art. I, § 8 (including portions of the Commerce Clause itself) would be surplusage
candidates.speaker: Thomas, concurring
phrases: An interpretation of cl. 3 that makes the rest of § 8 superfluous
